items.title: Singular cochain complex with coefficients
items.statement: $C^n(X;G)=\operatorname{Hom}(C_n(X;\mathbb Z),G)$ and $\delta\varphi=\varphi\partial$ in positive cohomological grading.
items.proof_strategy: Use integral singular chains and arbitrary abelian G; delta(phi)=phi boundary. Cochains are all functions on singular simplices, never finite-support functions. Degree n<0 is zero. For an R-module G identify with Hom_R(C_*(X;R),G) on the simplex basis.

items.title: The singular coboundary squares to zero
items.statement: $\delta^2\varphi=\varphi\partial^2=0$.
items.proof_strategy: Evaluate delta squared on every simplex and use boundary squared zero.

items.title: Singular cohomology with coefficients
items.statement: $H^n(X;G)=\ker\delta^n/\operatorname{im}\delta^{n-1}$, with $H^n=0$ for $n<0$.
items.proof_strategy: Take cycles modulo boundaries; the preceding lemma proves inclusion. Declare H^n=0 for n<0.

items.title: Singular cohomology is contravariantly functorial
items.statement: $f^*\varphi=\varphi f_*$ gives identity and composition laws on cohomology.
items.proof_strategy: Precomposition commutes with delta; verify contravariant composition and identities on representatives, also covariance in G.

items.title: Homotopic maps induce equal maps in singular cohomology
items.statement: dualising the prism chain homotopy gives a cochain homotopy.
items.proof_strategy: For g_*-f_*=boundary P+P boundary, K(phi)=phi P has degree -1 and g^*-f^*=delta K+K delta. The same formula preserves relative cochains for homotopies of pairs.

items.title: Relative singular cochain complex
items.statement: $C^*(X,A;G)=\operatorname{Hom}(C_*(X,A;\mathbb Z),G)$, equivalently cochains on $X$ vanishing on $A$.
items.proof_strategy: Relative groups are Hom(C_n(X)/C_n(A),G), identified with the kernel of restriction. The quotient has basis simplices not contained in A; define relative cohomology and maps of pairs here.

items.title: Restriction of singular cochains is degreewise split surjective
items.statement: Extend a cochain on A by zero on simplices not in A. This gives an additive section degree by degree, not a cochain-map section. The kernel is the relative cochain group.
items.proof_strategy: Extend a cochain on A by zero on simplices not in A. This gives an additive section degree by degree, not a cochain-map section. The kernel is the relative cochain group.

items.title: Long exact sequence of a pair in singular cohomology
items.statement: the short exact cochain sequence yields the contravariantly ordered LES and explicit connector.
items.proof_strategy: Use the split-in-each-degree sequence 0 -> C^*(X,A) -> C^*(X) -> C^*(A) -> 0. Connector sends a cocycle to the coboundary of an extension. Prove extension and representative independence, and include n=0 and the empty pair.

items.title: Naturality of the singular cohomology pair sequence
items.statement: maps of pairs commute with restrictions and connecting maps.
items.proof_strategy: Compare pullback of any lift with any lift of the pullback; their difference is relative. Thus restrictions and the degree +1 connector commute for every map of pairs.

items.title: Excision for singular cohomology
items.statement: under $\overline Z\subseteq\operatorname{int}A$, restriction induces $H^*(X,A;G)\cong H^*(X-Z,A-Z;G)$.
items.proof_strategy: Dualize actual subdivision retraction and homotopy, not a bare homology equivalence. With B=X-Z, interiors of A and B cover X. Compare pair cochain sequences for C(A)+C(B) and C(X); use the five lemma and identify quotient by C(A) with C(B)/C(A intersection B). Closure(Z) subset interior(A) is essential.

items.title: Mayer vietoris sequence in singular cohomology
items.statement: an open cover $X=U\cup V$ gives the cohomological LES with difference of restrictions and its natural connector.
items.proof_strategy: For an open cover X=U union V, use 0 -> Hom(C(U)+C(V),G) -> C^*(U;G) direct-sum C^*(V;G) -> C^*(U intersection V;G) -> 0. Last map is restriction from U minus restriction from V. Extend cochains by zero to prove surjectivity; identify small and full cohomology using the actual chain homotopy equivalence. Print the degree +1 connector and naturality.

items.title: Kronecker evaluation pairing
items.statement: $\langle[\varphi],[c]\rangle=\varphi(c)$ pairs $H^n(X;G)$ with $H_n(X;\mathbb Z)$.
items.proof_strategy: Define evaluation first on cocycles and cycles; quotient descent is justified by the following lemma. Give the relative version too.

items.title: The kronecker pairing is independent of cocycle and cycle representatives
items.statement: coboundaries vanish on cycles and cocycles vanish on boundaries.
items.proof_strategy: For a cocycle phi, cycle c, cochain psi and chain b, compute (phi+delta psi)(c+boundary b)=phi(c). Include bilinearity and <f^*phi,c>=<phi,f_*c>.

items.title: Topological universal coefficient short exact sequence for cohomology
items.statement: applying the HA theorem gives $0\to\operatorname{Ext}(H_{n-1}(X),G)\to H^n(X;G)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_n(X),G)\to0$, naturally in $X,G$.
items.proof_strategy: Assume Choice as required by the imported algebra. Singular absolute and relative chain groups are free over Z. Apply the algebraic UCT and identify its evaluation edge map with the Kronecker map. State naturality in pairs and in G. Ext means Ext^1_Z and has degree n-1, with H_-1=0.

items.title: Cohomology over a field is dual to homology over that field
items.statement: over a field $k$, $H^n(X;k)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H_n(X;k),k)$ naturally under the stated chain hypotheses.
items.proof_strategy: Apply the arbitrary-rank algebraic UCT over k, not the finite-dimensional corollary. Use the simplex-basis identification Hom_Z(C_Z,k)=Hom_k(C_k,k); Ext vanishes. No finiteness assumption on X or H_n.

items.title: Integral cohomology detects adjacent homology torsion
items.statement: for finitely generated homology, the torsion in $H^n(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the torsion of $H_{n-1}(X;\mathbb Z)$.
items.proof_strategy: For finitely generated H_n and H_(n-1), evaluate Hom and Ext on finite cyclic decompositions. Identify torsion subgroup abstractly with torsion of H_(n-1); do not claim a canonical self-duality of finite torsion groups.

items.title: Topological kunneth short exact sequence for homology
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a PID $R$, arbitrary spaces $X,Y$, and $n\geq0$, there is a short exact sequence, natural in continuous maps of both spaces, $0\to\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H_p(X;R)\otimes_R H_q(Y;R)\to H_n(X\times Y;R)\to\bigoplus_{p+q=n-1}\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(H_p(X;R),H_q(Y;R))\to0$. Indices are nonnegative; empty sums are zero. The left arrow is induced by the singular shuffle cross product.
items.proof_strategy: BLOCKED on the proposed HA supplier pair. Under Choice and a PID R, C(X;R), C(Y;R) are nonnegative free complexes with finite diagonals in every total degree. Transport the tensor/Tor sequence along the shuffle chain homotopy equivalence; identify the left arrow on cycle tensors. Natural exact sequence, not a natural decomposition.

items.title: Cohomological kunneth isomorphism under finite free hypotheses
items.statement: the cohomology cross product is an isomorphism when one factor has degreewise finite free homology over the PID, with the full hypothesis printed.
items.proof_strategy: Assume Choice, R a PID, arbitrary spaces X,Y, and H_q(Y;R) degreewise finite free. Replace C(Y;R) by the zero-differential complex H_*(Y;R) using the preceding lemma. Hom-tensor comparison is an isomorphism for each finite-free H_q(Y), and each degree has finitely many p,q>=0. This proves the additive cross-product isomorphism without ring structure or CW approximation. Finiteness of singular CHAIN groups is neither assumed nor true. items.title: Integral cohomology of real projective space from uct
items.statement: computes every group and tracks the one-degree torsion shift.
items.proof_strategy: For RP^m: H^0=Z; H^q=Z/2 for even q with 0<q<=m; H^m=Z if m odd; all remaining positive groups zero. Separate m=0; for RP^infinity the even positive pattern continues. Recompute cellular homology in the local A supplier, never import a B-only example.

items.statement: exhibits a product degree where the Tor summand is nonzero.

items.statement: torsion in adjacent homology produces an Ext class pairing trivially with $H_n$.

items.title: The uct splitting is not natural
items.statement: a source-standard map of finitely generated groups defeats a functorial choice.
items.proof_strategy: Use Hatcher section 3.1 Exercise 11(a): degree-m Moore space M= S^n union_m e^(n+1), n>=1,m>=2, quotient q:M->S^(n+1). Reduced integral homology map is zero but q^*:Z->Z/m is reduction mod m. Compute the latter via relative cochains/connector or prove the cellular cochain comparison first. Naturality of a UCT section would force q^*=0 since the Hom summand on M vanishes. A bare map of finitely generated groups alone does not prove topological nonnaturality.
